app.title: Title and abstract screening for a systematic review
app.summary: The screener works through database records one at a time after duplicates across sources have been removed, reading each title, author list, venue and abstract with inclusion terms shaded and exclusion flags underlined from keyword lists they can edit. They include, exclude or mark maybe from the keyboard, choosing an exclusion reason from the protocol's list by number, and can add a note. A queue filter lets them go back through only the maybes or jump to the next unscreened record, while a progress bar and running counts give the numbers a flow diagram needs. They export a CSV with one row per exported record, duplicates included and marked, under their initials so two screeners' files line up for an agreement check.

task.text: Decide quickly, from the keyboard, which literature records go on to full-text review and why the rest are excluded, keeping the counts the review must report.

data.text: Bibliographic records exported from several literature databases, each with title, authors, venue, year and abstract, plus the screener's decision, exclusion reason, note and time for each.
data.item: one bibliographic record with its abstract

stage.text: title and abstract screening before full-text review

mechanism.text: A single-record view is driven by a filterable queue and keyboard keys for include, exclude-with-numbered-reason and maybe, each decision advancing to the next record; editable keyword lists shade and flag terms in the record as it is shown. A side column keeps running counts by decision and reason, and the decisions export as one CSV row per record.

field.text: systematic literature review in health informatics

workflow.name: triage a collection one item at a time

steps.step: remove duplicate items before working through them
steps.here: Records from several database exports are matched by title, ignoring case and punctuation; later copies are dropped from the queue, counted, and noted on the record that was kept.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: One record at a time shows its id, source, year, venue, title, authors and abstract with a 'Record n of m' position; arrow keys or buttons move back and forward, and each decision advances to the next record.

steps.step: highlight the terms that bear on the decision
steps.here: Two editable comma-separated lists shade inclusion terms and dash-underline exclusion flags in the title and abstract, matching plurals and trailing-* wildcards, with a line listing which terms were found and how often.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: i includes and m marks maybe; e opens the six exclusion reasons from the protocol, picked with 1 to 6, with Esc to back out; / jumps to a free-text note for the record.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A bar shows how many records are screened, and a side table keeps the PRISMA flow counts: identified per source, duplicates removed, screened, excluded by each reason, included, maybe and not yet screened.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A queue filter restricts the pass to all, not screened, maybe, included or excluded records, so the maybes can be revisited, and n jumps to the next record without a decision.

A CSV download has one row per exported record, duplicates included and marked with the record they duplicate, giving decision, reason, note, time and the screener's initials, which also go in the file name.

distinctive: Duplicates across database exports are removed by normalised title before screening, and the number removed is reported, as the systematic-review flow diagram requires.
An exclusion cannot be recorded without one of the protocol's six reasons, chosen by number key so the whole pass runs from the keyboard.
Two separate term lists mark likely-inclusion words and likely-exclusion flags differently, and the screener edits them as spelling variants turn up.
The export keeps one row per exported record, duplicates included, with screener initials, so two screeners' independent files join by record id for an agreement statistic.

parts.title: Queue filter and navigation
parts.summary: Restricts the queue to all, unscreened, maybe, included or excluded records and moves to the previous, next or next unscreened record, advancing automatically after each decision.

spans.first: .queue-bar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; font-size: 13px; }
function queue() { return state.filter === "all" ? SCREEN : SCREEN.filter((r) => statusOf(r.id) === state.filter); }

parts.title: Decision bar and exclusion reasons
parts.summary: Records include, exclude or maybe for the current record by button or key, with exclude opening the protocol's numbered reasons and Escape backing out.
